name: New York City: Retail
law: NYC Fair Workweek Law (retail on-call scheduling)

coverage.summary: Retail businesses with 20 or more employees that are primarily engaged in selling consumer goods at one or more stores in New York City.
coverage.employees: All full-time, part-time and temporary employees of a covered retail employer.
notes: "Primarily engaged" means more than half of the business's NYC sales in the previous 12 months were consumer goods sold to retail customers (6 RCNY § 7-601).
Local Law 77 of 2021 extended the same rules to utility safety employees.

citation.quote: A retail employer shall provide a retail employee with a written work schedule no later than 72 hours before the first shift on the work schedule.

prohibitions.label: Shift cancelled or cut within 72 hours of its start

citation.quote: A retail employer shall not cancel any regular shift of a retail employee within 72 hours of the scheduled start of such shift. Cutting more than 15 minutes without 72 hours' notice is a cancellation.

prohibitions.label: Required to work hours added with less than 72 hours' notice

citation.quote: A retail employer shall not require a retail employee to work with fewer than 72 hours' notice, unless the employee consents in writing.

exceptions.label: I asked for the time off
exceptions.description: The employee requested the time off.

exceptions.label: I traded shifts with a coworker
exceptions.description: The change was a shift trade between employees.

exceptions.label: The store couldn't open or stay open
exceptions.description: Operations could not begin or continue because of threats, a utility failure or public transit shutdown, fire, flood or other natural disaster, or a declared state of emergency.

exceptions.label: I agreed in writing to work the added hours
exceptions.description: The employee consented in writing to work hours added with less than 72 hours' notice.

otherRights.label: No on-call shifts, and no being told to call in to find out if you work within 72 hours of a shift
For a late cancellation, relief must include the pay for the time you were scheduled but didn't work

enforcement.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)

sources.title: DCWP Fair Workweek rules, 6 RCNY Ch. 7 Subch. F

notes: NYC's retail law has no predictability pay. Shiftowed flags prohibited changes as violations you can report; the agency can order back pay and damages.
Shiftowed checks the 72-hour posting rule against the first day a schedule covers. The law measures it to the first shift, which may be later.
